inputs.text: Abinader’s government is putting the Dominican Republic on a path shaped by OECD “global standards,” with Roberto Álvarez and Mathias Cormann signing an agreement in Paris on 25 March 2026 to design the country’s first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy. Fighting corruption is worthwhile, but it should strengthen accountable Dominican institutions—not become a pretext for handing more influence to international bureaucrats. The real test will be whether this produces honest government at home, rather than another polished agreement abroad.
